title: Structure sheaf and quasi-coherent algebras on an algebraic stack
statement: Work in the universe and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $p:\mathcal X\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ be a category fibred in groupoids in the sense of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; for instance an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], or the $2$-fibre product $\mathcal Z\times_VW$ of an algebraic stack $\mathcal Z$ with a scheme $W$ over an algebraic space $V$. No algebraicity is used in the constructions below. Its big fppf site, with site and sheaf terminology as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], has objects $x\in\mathcal X(T)$, morphisms the arrows of the fibred category, and covering families those whose underlying scheme maps form fppf covering families [def-pc-fppf-site]. The structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}(x)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, with restriction along an arrow over $u:T'\to T$ the pullback of regular functions. Here $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)=\mathcal O_T(T)$ denotes sections on the whole scheme; the pullback is the component over $T$ of the structure-sheaf morphism of $u$. A sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-algebras is a sheaf $\mathcal A$ of commutative rings on this site (its underlying presheaf of sets satisfies the sheaf condition, and its ring operations commute with restrictions) with a morphism of ring sheaves $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal A$; its morphisms are ring-sheaf morphisms commuting with these structure maps. It is quasi-coherent when its underlying $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with action $r\cdot a=\eta(r)a$ for its structure morphism $\eta$, is quasi-coherent on this ringed site in the general site sense of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]: locally it has an exact presentation $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}^{(I)}\to\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}^{(J)}\to\mathcal A\to0$ for small sets $I,J$. A surjection of such algebras means a morphism locally surjective as a map of sheaves: every section of the target lifts after an fppf covering of its domain. Global sections $\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ are compatible families of sections over all objects of the site, equivalently morphisms from the terminal sheaf to the underlying sheaf of sets of $\mathcal A$; the ring operations are pointwise. The same convention defines global sections of any sheaf on this site. If $Y$ is an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ is a functor over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ to the discrete fibred category of $Y$ (objects over $T$ are maps $T\to Y$, with arrows given by commutative triangles), write $\mathcal X_W=\mathcal X\times_YW$ for the $2$-fibre product [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. The direct-image sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ is given by $(\phi_*\mathcal A)(W\to Y)=\Gamma(\mathcal X_W,\mathcal A|_{\mathcal X_W})$ for etale schemes $W\to Y$, with restrictions induced by base change. Here restriction to $\mathcal X_W$ means precomposition with its projection $q:\mathcal X_W\to\mathcal X$: on an object $(x,w,\alpha)$ over a scheme $T$ its value is $\mathcal A(x)$, with the original restrictions and algebra operations. Its structure morphism has source $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, exactly the value of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_W}$ on that object. The canonical map $\mathcal O_Y\to\phi_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ sends a regular function on $W$ to its pullback on $\mathcal X_W$.
